subject: Brightlane: capacity gating & final swap playbook
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Turner <leah@brightlane.ai>, Theo Alvarez <theo@brightlane.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Brightlane: capacity gating & final swap playbook

Leah / Theo —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our commercial commit (DL-2026-0193) we need to lock the final swap window and validate sizing for the Dedicated pool before we flip production traffic. I attached an initial playbook and the capacity model (see attachments).

Summary of asks: 
- Confirm a 4-hour maintenance window: preferred 2026-09-16 02:00–06:00 PT (can shift +/- 2 hours).
- Approve the preflight tests (outlined in section 2 of the playbook).
- Share any traffic anomalies/expected surge signals for the first 48 hrs post-swap.

Acceptance criteria (short):
- 95th pctl P99 gen latency on your peak path within agreed SLA during a staged 30m soak with 2x expected concurrency.
- No more than 2% token error rate increase vs hosted baseline across evaluation prompts.
- Autoscale thresholds validated and failover route tested.

Attachments in this thread:
- brightlane_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook + runbook)
- capacity_model_20260910.csv (traffic model + GPU mapping)

If that window works, we’ll circulate the swap checklist and schedule a dry-run preflight on 2026-09-15.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: Leah Turner <leah@brightlane.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.ai, theo@brightlane.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane: capacity gating & final swap playbook

Hannah —

Thanks, this looks good. 2026-09-16 02:00–06:00 PT is acceptable. Procurement is on copy to confirm any calendar-level approvals. We’ll run the traffic patterns you requested against our canary cluster and share results by EOD 9/15.

A couple of notes from our side: 
- We expect a marketing-driven increase in requests between 09/16 08:00–12:00 PT (after the swap) — roughly +30% burst for 2 hours. Recommend we validate scale-to and burst scenarios.
- Our security team asked whether the MOP includes a rollback path that preserves inference logs for audit; can you confirm?

I’ll circulate the signed MOP when procurement completes the DocuSign routing.

—Leah
Leah Turner
Head of Platform, Brightlane AI
leah@brightlane.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane: capacity gating & final swap playbook

Hannah / team —

I reviewed the capacity_model_20260910.csv and sketched two adjustments based on their burst note:
1) Increase reserved GPU headroom by +15% on the primary pod (adds 2x A100-80GB equivalence).
2) Configure temporary burst queue on a secondary pool for 4 hours post-swap with a soft cap and throttling policy.

Preflight plan (quick):
- 09/15 03:00–03:45 PT: 30m staged soak at 1.5x concurrency (smoke + perf traces).
- 09/15 04:00–04:30 PT: 30m latency stress with 2x concurrency and evaluation prompts.
- Validate cache warmup time and KV hit ratio (target > 85% after warmup).

Metrics to record: p50/p95/p99 gen latency, GPU utilization, batch size distribution, tokens/sec, error% by prompt set.

I’ll prepare a compact validation dashboard for the preflight and drop the runbook link into the hubspot deal. If the preflight fails any hard gate, we stop and revert to the hosted route while we adjust sizing.

Ben — can you confirm ops availability for the swap window and who will run the rollback step if needed?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: ops-team@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Leah Turner <leah@brightlane.ai>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Brightlane: capacity gating & final swap playbook

Forwarding final playbook and checklist to Ops for scheduling the dry-run and the production swap. Please use the attached swap_checklist_v3.xlsx and follow the rollback preservation steps described under section 4.2 — that preserves inference logs to a secure bucket for audit.

DocuSign status: Leah’s procurement routed the MOP; expected signed copy by 9/15 EOD. Link: https://www.docusign.com/signed/brightlane-mop

Preflight ops points: 
- Run the staged soak at 03:00 PT 09/15 and confirm KV cache warmup < 15m.
- Execute synthetic burst at 04:00 PT to validate secondary pool spill behavior.
- Ensure alerting thresholds are set so we get a 1-minute notification on P99 degradation > 25%.

Attachments: swap_checklist_v3.xlsx, brightlane_playbook_v1.pdf

/Hannah
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Leah Turner <leah@brightlane.ai>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane: capacity gating & final swap playbook

Hannah / team —

All green from Ops. Dry-run completed 09/15 per checklist: KV warmup ~12m, 30m soak at 1.5x concurrency passed, synthetic burst resulted in graceful spill to secondary pool with throttling kicking in at expected thresholds. No regression in token error rates observed.

We have the signed MOP attached: signed_mop_brightlane.pdf.

We’ll stand by for the scheduled swap on 09/16 02:00 PT. I’ll lead the production swap and will alert on the final go/no-go at T-20.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
